recent_posts.title: Talking About Pulumi and Network Automation
recent_posts.summary: Scott Lowe appeared on the Network Automagic podcast to discuss Pulumi, what it is, and how it fits into a broader network automation framework. recent_posts.title: Using Mitmproxy to Observe kubectl Traffic
recent_posts.summary: A step-by-step guide on using mitmproxy to intercept and observe HTTPS traffic between kubectl and the Kubernetes API server. The setup involves extracting client certificates from a Kubeconfig file using yq and base64, then launching mitmproxy with specific flags to disable HTTP/2, supply the client cert, and skip upstream TLS verification. kubectl is then run with HTTPS_PROXY pointing to the local mitmproxy instance. The technique is presented as useful for troubleshooting rather than as a learning tool.

recent_posts.title: Running the Azure CLI in a Container
recent_posts.summary: Running the Azure CLI in a standard Docker container as an alias turns out to be surprisingly painful: you need to mount config and SSH directories, and files end up owned by root. The author explores this approach, hits multiple friction points, then discovers Distrobox as a cleaner solution. Distrobox shares the host home directory automatically, so no volume mounts are needed. The workflow is: create a Distrobox container (Debian 13), install the Azure CLI inside it, then export the binary to the host with `distrobox-export`. The result is a clean host system with the Azure CLI fully accessible as if installed natively.

recent_posts.title: Setting up a VPC Route Server with Pulumi
recent_posts.summary: A step-by-step guide to creating an AWS VPC Route Server using Pulumi and Go. Covers the creation sequence: Route Server with ASN configuration, VPC association, endpoint creation in a subnet, route table propagation, and BGP peer setup. Includes explicit dependency management using pulumi.DependsOn to avoid resource creation errors. Provides AWS CLI commands for verification and mentions potential BGP peers like Cilium CNI or FRR daemon.
